name: Oscar Wilde
bio: Dublin-born writer; born 16 October 1854 at 21 Westland Row, educated at Trinity College Dublin and Magdalen College, Oxford. Married Constance Lloyd on 29 May 1884; two sons, Cyril (b. 1885) and Vyvyan (b. 1886). Convicted 25 May 1895 and sentenced to two years' hard labour following the three trials of that spring; released 19 May 1897 and lived thereafter in France and Italy. Died 30 November 1900 at the Hôtel d'Alsace, Paris, of cerebral meningitis; buried at Bagneux, moved to Père Lachaise in 1909.
bio_note: All facts from the Chronological Table, Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000), pp. viii-xii (repo PDF 8-12), read as page images 2026-08-03.
roster_note: The collective 'unnamed and one-scene companions' entry was removed 2026-08-04: every named man in it now has his own node and edge (Andre, Pietro, le petit Georges, the Napoule fisherman, the Cafe d'Egypte Egyptian, Raphael, Fortune, the Naples 'Sea-God'), so the entry only duplicated them. TWO THINGS IT CARRIED HAVE NO NODE: (1) the unnamed 'beautiful boy in grey velvet' seen with Wilde outside a cafe behind the Madeleine by Aleck Ross, late March 1900 (Complete Letters printed 1177) - a roster candidate on exactly the same footing as the Sea-God and the Napoule fisherman, who are already nodes; and (2) Wilde's general remark on the Riviera fishing population, 27 December 1898 (printed 1112), which is a remark rather than a person. Full transcriptions remain in dossiers/EXILE-COMPANIONS_dossier.md (T1-T4).
